Based on the search results, here's what I found about ChartMuseum, the NeurIPS 2025 chart visual reasoning benchmark:

## Overview

ChartMuseum is a chart question answering benchmark designed to evaluate reasoning capabilities of large vision-language models (LVLMs) over real-world chart images. It contains 1,162 expert-annotated questions spanning multiple reasoning types, curated from real-world charts across 184 sources, specifically built to evaluate complex visual and textual reasoning.

## Key Features

ChartMuseum was created by 13 computer science researchers and consists of 1,162 (image, question, answer) tuples sourced from 928 unique real-world images across 184 websites. Unlike prior benchmarks where questions are typically model-generated and later refined by annotators, all questions in ChartMuseum were curated by researchers without assistance from LLMs. Each question underwent a manual multi-stage review process to ensure question quality and answer objectivity.

## Benchmark Results

Although humans achieve 93% accuracy, the best-performing model Gemini-2.5-Pro attains only 63.0%, and the leading open-source LVLM Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct achieves only 38.5%. 

On questions requiring primarily visual reasoning, all models experience a 35%-55% performance drop from text-reasoning-heavy question performance.

## Question Categories

Questions are categorized into four types: Textual reasoning questions can be solved almost exclusively with textual reasoning, visual reasoning questions are most easily answerable from visual aspects of the chart, text/visual reasoning questions can be answered by either primarily text or primarily visual reasoning, and synthesis reasoning questions require both textual and visual reasoning.

The benchmark is available on GitHub and Hugging Face, with evaluation code provided for assessing model performance.

## Overview

ChartMuseum is a chart question answering benchmark designed to evaluate reasoning capabilities of large vision-language models (LVLMs) over real-world chart images. It contains 1,162 expert-annotated questions spanning multiple reasoning types, curated from real-world charts across 184 sources, specifically built to evaluate complex visual and textual reasoning.

## Key Features

ChartMuseum was created by 13 computer science researchers and consists of 1,162 (image, question, answer) tuples sourced from 928 unique real-world images across 184 websites. Unlike prior benchmarks where questions are typically model-generated and later refined by annotators, all questions in ChartMuseum were curated by researchers without assistance from LLMs. Each question underwent a manual multi-stage review process to ensure question quality and answer objectivity.

## Benchmark Results

Although humans achieve 93% accuracy, the best-performing model Gemini-2.5-Pro attains only 63.0%, and the leading open-source LVLM Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct achieves only 38.5%. 

On questions requiring primarily visual reasoning, all models experience a 35%-55% performance drop from text-reasoning-heavy question performance.

## Question Categories

Questions are categorized into four types: Textual reasoning questions can be solved almost exclusively with textual reasoning, visual reasoning questions are most easily answerable from visual aspects of the chart, text/visual reasoning questions can be answered by either primarily text or primarily visual reasoning, and synthesis reasoning questions require both textual and visual reasoning.

The benchmark is available on GitHub and Hugging Face, with evaluation code provided for assessing model performance.

## Chart-RL Overview

Chart-RL is an extension of the open-source VLM-R1 platform that adapts R1-style reinforcement fine-tuning for chart understanding tasks. It is an efficient reinforcement fine-tuning framework that employs R1-style reinforcement learning to enhance chart understanding capabilities in Vision Language Models (VLMs).

## Key Innovation

A key insight motivating the approach is that chart-based questions frequently correspond to mathematically verifiable ground truths, making them well-suited for rule-based reward functions in RL training. The framework leverages group relative policy optimization (GRPO) with chart-aligned accuracy and format rewards.

## Technical Components

Chart-RL implements a verifiable reward function that produces a score based on alignment between model outputs and annotated ground truths, and a binary format reward function is employed to enforce task-specific output structures. The framework employs the GRPO algorithm, which evaluates a group of candidate responses to guide policy updates, eliminating the need for a separate critic.

## Performance Results

Chart-RL consistently outperforms supervised fine-tuning (SFT) across different chart understanding benchmarks, achieving relative improvements of 16.7% on MutlChartQA and 11.5% on ChartInsights. Chart-RL trained on merely 10 complex chart-query examples significantly outperforms models trained on over 6,000 simple examples.

## Overview

ChartPoint proposes PointCoT, which integrates reflective interaction into chain-of-thought reasoning in charts. By prompting MLLMs to generate bounding boxes and re-render charts based on location annotations, it establishes connections between textual reasoning steps and visual grounding.

## The Problem Being Addressed

MLLMs exhibit weak grounding in chart elements and proportional relationships, as evidenced by their inability to localize key positions to match their reasoning.

## Dataset and Models

ChartPoint introduces an automated pipeline to construct ChartPoint-SFT-62k, a dataset featuring 19.2K high-quality chart samples with step-by-step CoT, bounding box, and re-rendered visualizations. Two instruction-tuned models, ChartPoint_Q2 and ChartPoint_Q2.5, outperform state-of-the-art across several chart benchmarks, e.g., +5.04% on ChartBench.

## Methodology

After obtaining the bounding boxes for all grounding steps, the instruction data with location annotations is constructed, which primarily includes four formats and 62K Q&A pairs. The approach includes different task types: standard VQA tasks and localization tasks where bounding boxes serve as ground truth instead of answers.

## Key Findings:

**Chart and Visualization Grounding:**
Vision-Language Models (VLMs) frequently misread values, hallucinate details, and confuse overlapping elements in charts. Current approaches rely solely on pixel interpretation, creating a Pixel-Only Bottleneck: agents treat interactive charts as static images, losing access to the structured specification that encodes exact values.

Introspective and Interactive Visual Grounding (IVG) combines spec-grounded introspection, which queries the underlying specification for deterministic evidence, with view-grounded interaction, which manipulates the view to resolve visual ambiguity. iPlotBench is a benchmark of 500 interactive Plotly figures with 6,706 binary questions and ground-truth specifications.

**GUI and Pixel Coordinate Grounding:**
GUI grounding, the task of mapping natural-language instructions to pixel coordinates, is crucial for autonomous agents, yet remains difficult for current VLMs. The core bottleneck is reliable patch-to-pixel mapping, which breaks when extrapolating to high-resolution displays unseen during training.

Ruler tokens serve as explicit coordinate markers, letting the model reference positions similar to gridlines on a map and adjust rather than generate coordinates from scratch. Interleaved MRoPE (I-MRoPE) improves spatial encoding by ensuring that width and height dimensions are represented equally.

**VLM Training Signals:**

## Visionary-R1 Overview

Visionary-R1 is the official implementation of the paper 'Visionary-R1: Mitigating Shortcuts in Visual Reasoning with Reinforcement Learning'. When trained on 273K CoT-free visual question-answer pairs and using only reinforcement learning, Visionary-R1 outperforms strong multimodal models, such as GPT-4o, Claude3.5-Sonnet, and Gemini-1.5-Pro, on multiple visual reasoning benchmarks.

## Caption-Reason-Answer Format

The core approach uses a structured training format: The cornerstone of this approach is a structured caption–reason–answer training format, where the model must first generate a detailed caption of the image before proceeding to reasoning and answering the question.

## Caption Reward

To further ensure that the captions are meaningful and informative, reinforcement learning from AI feedback is applied, involving a caption reward, which is combined with standard accuracy and format rewards. More specifically, the policy model's LLM part is used to answer questions based on the description between the info tags, serving as the caption rewards.

The caption reward is a binary reward where only the caption is provided as model input, and the predicted answer must still be correct; this assesses the informativeness and relevance of the generated caption.

## Impact and Results

Enforcing the caption–reason–answer format yields substantial gains over vanilla RL, and the caption reward further enhances both in-domain and transfer accuracy.

## "Beyond Pixels: Introspective and Interactive Grounding for Visualization Agents"

The paper presents Introspective and Interactive Visual Grounding (IVG), a framework that gives visualization agents structured access to their own outputs.

### Key Components:

**IVG Framework:** IVG combines (1) spec-grounded introspection, which queries the underlying specification for deterministic evidence, with (2) view-grounded interaction, which manipulates the view to resolve visual ambiguity.

**iPlotBench Benchmark:** iPlotBench is a benchmark of 500 interactive Plotly figures with 6,706 binary questions, ground-truth specifications, and Semantic Structural Similarity for deterministic evaluation.

### Implementation:

IVG is implemented as a Visualization State API using Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, allowing any compatible agent to access these capabilities.
